record.original_question: For asymptotic expansions of minimal discrete energies on the sphere, can one establish further relations between coefficients appearing in expansions for different energies, such as logarithmic energy and Riesz s-energy?

evidence.quote: Question 2.1 (Johann Brauchart). Can other relation be established between coefficients of different (w.r.t energy) asymptotic expansions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{S}^d \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ denote the unit sphere. For a configuration $\omega_N = \{x_1,\dots,x_N\} \subset \mathbb{S}^d$ of $N$ distinct points, define the Riesz $s$-energy ($s>0$, $s\neq 0$) by
$$E_s(\omega_N) = \sum_{i\neq j} \frac{1}{\|x_i - x_j\|^s},$$
and the logarithmic energy by
$$E_{\log}(\omega_N) = \sum_{i\neq j} \log\frac{1}{\|x_i - x_j\|}.$$
Let $\mathcal{E}_s(\mathbb{S}^d, N) = \min_{\omega_N} E_s(\omega_N)$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(\mathbb{S}^d, N) = \min_{\omega_N} E_{\log}(\omega_N)$ denote the minimal energies. As $N\to\infty$, these admit asymptotic expansions of the form
$$\mathcal{E}_s(\mathbb{S}^d, N) = V_s(\mathbb{S}^d) N^2 + C_{s,d}\, N^{1+s/d} + \text{lower order terms} \quad (0<s<d),$$
$$\mathcal{E}_s(\mathbb{S}^d, N) = -\tfrac{1}{d}N^2 \log N + C_{d,d}\, N^2 + \text{lower order terms} \quad (s=d),$$
$$\mathcal{E}_s(\mathbb{S}^d, N) = C_{s,d}\, N^{1+s/d} + \text{higher order terms} \quad (s>d),$$
$$\mathcal{E}_{\log}(\mathbb{S}^d, N) = W_{\log}(\mathbb{S}^d) N^2 - \tfrac{1}{d} N \log N + C_{\log,d}\, N + o(N),$$
with further (mostly conjectural) terms of lower order. The leading-order constants and several next-order constants are known to be related across the different values of $s$ (and to the logarithmic case) via analytic continuation of zeta-function-type expressions.

Problem: Establish further (proved) relations between the coefficients appearing in the asymptotic expansions of $\mathcal{E}_s(\mathbb{S}^d, N)$ for distinct values of $s$, and between those coefficients and the coefficients in the expansion of $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(\mathbb{S}^d, N)$, beyond the relations currently known.
artifact.category_tag: Minimal energy point configurations on spheres
artifact.status_search_result: The question of relating coefficients across different Riesz $s$-energy and logarithmic energy expansions on the sphere remains an active area. Conjectured closed-form expressions (e.g., for the next-order constant in the logarithmic case by Brauchart–Hardin–Saff, derived under analytic continuation assumptions) are not proved in general, and only one or two terms of these expansions are rigorously known on $\mathbb{S}^d$ for $d\ge 2$. No general framework establishing further proved relations between these coefficients appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: The next-order term for optimal Riesz and logarithmic energy asymptotics on the sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectures for the next-order term are based on analytic continuation assumptions (with respect to s) for the coefficients in the asymptotic expansion of the optimal s-energy.
status_evidence.claim: Relations between coefficients of different energy expansions on the sphere are conjectural, based on analytic continuation.

status_evidence.title: Renormalized Energy and Asymptotic Expansion of Optimal Logarithmic Energy on the Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Bétermin–Sandier proved existence of the order-n term in the logarithmic energy expansion on S^2; the closed-form value conjectured by Brauchart–Hardin–Saff remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-order coefficients on S^2 are still conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Distributing many points on spheres: minimal energy and designs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing known and conjectured terms in minimal energy asymptotic expansions and relations among them.
status_evidence.claim: Establishing further relations among coefficients across energies remains an open research direction.
